description: Proposal of Application Notice for a data centre (Major development) at the former IBM site, Spango Valley, Inverkip Road, Greenock, by Slate Island Developments Ltd. Developer states PAN submitted 27 February 2026; research brief cites 24 February 2026 — both retained pending portal verification. Statutory pre-application consultation: public exhibitions at Branchton Community Centre 24 March and 23 April 2026; online events 26 March and 28 April 2026.

events.title: PAN submitted to Inverclyde Council (developer-stated date)
First public exhibition, Branchton Community Centre (4 attendees per developer)
First online interactive event (0 attendees per developer)
Second public exhibition, Branchton Community Centre

decision_notes: Official PAN reference could not be verified: Inverclyde Council's Idox portal (planning.inverclyde.gov.uk/online-applications/) returned HTTP 503 on 2026-07-30 and no secondary source publishes the reference. Developer targets Major application submission June 2026 and determination November 2026; no evidence of submission found by 30 July 2026.

description: Planning permission in principle for four data-centre buildings totalling approximately 80,000 sqm, with energy centre and electrical infrastructure, access, drainage, landscaping and associated works at the former IBM site, Spango Valley.
decision_notes: Pending consideration on 3 September 2026. The portal displayed 1,456 comments and 33 documents at that check; both totals can change. Applicant listed as Slate Islands Development Ltd and agent as Pegasus Group.

representations.notes: Portal displayed 1,456 public comments. The interface did not establish an objection/support split, so this is a comments total rather than a verified objection count.

events.title: Application validated and opened for comment

description: Proposed Section 36 (Electricity Act 1989) application for a c.99 MW battery energy storage system co-located with the data centre, including 132kV and 33kV substations, inverter/transformer stations, control rooms, 120,000-litre water tank and SuDS pond. Consultation held jointly with the data centre PAN to satisfy both Electricity Act and Town and Country Planning Act pre-application requirements.
decision_notes: No ECU case reference located; application not yet found on the ECU portal as of 2026-07-30.

description: Prior consent context: Planning Permission in Principle for a £100m housing-led mixed-use scheme (up to 450 homes, commercial/leisure/community/retail, park-and-ride at the former IBM rail halt), applied for February 2020 by Barton Willmore for Sandy Easdale, James Easdale and Advance Construction. Planning board initially capped housing at 270 homes; the 450-home upper limit was agreed and permission finalised March 2023. Developer states marketing failed to secure a viable end user, prompting the 2026 data centre/BESS pivot.
decision_notes: Decision date approximate (March 2023 per Wikipedia and press; exact date and reference not verified — council committee papers reference case 22/0225/IC in 2022, unconfirmed as this PPP). Whether this consent remains extant alongside the data centre proposal is unresolved.
